item.content:encoded:
Are you a professor, researcher, or academic looking for an opportunity to expand your international research experience, teach at a leading university in France, and connect with scholars from around the world? The Sciences Po Visiting Faculty Opportunities 2027–2028 provide an opportunity for outstanding academics to spend a semester at Sciences Po in Paris, where they can conduct research, teach, participate in academic activities, and become part of an international research community.

Every year, Sciences Po welcomes around 100 researchers and professors from different parts of the world. During their stays, visiting academics are integrated into the university’s research and academic activities, allowing them to interact with researchers, contribute to teaching, participate in seminars and research events, and develop international academic networks.

The available calls cover different academic disciplines and geographic backgrounds. Some opportunities are open to outstanding candidates from all disciplines and all continents, while other programmes are specifically designed for academics affiliated with particular universities, countries, or regions.

For the 2027–2028 academic year, several of the listed visiting faculty opportunities have an application deadline of 15 November 2026.

About Sciences Po Visiting Faculty Opportunities

Sciences Po is a major institution of higher education and research in France, with a strong international orientation and a long-standing focus on research, teaching, public policy, social sciences, political science, economics, international affairs, law, and other fields.

Through its Visiting Faculty programmes, Sciences Po provides researchers and professors with an opportunity to temporarily join its academic environment.

A visiting faculty member is expected to contribute to the university rather than simply use its facilities for independent research. Visiting academics are integrated into the research community they join and are expected to participate actively in academic activities.

This makes the opportunity particularly valuable for academics who want to combine:

  • International research experience
  • University-level teaching
  • Academic networking
  • Research collaboration
  • Knowledge exchange
  • Public academic engagement
  • Professional development

The exact conditions, including financial arrangements, can vary depending on the individual programme. Applicants should therefore carefully review the specific call for applications before applying.

What Do Visiting Faculty Members Do at Sciences Po?

Visiting faculty members are expected to contribute to both the teaching and research missions of the university.

During their stay, visiting professors are generally expected to teach one full course per semester.

A typical course usually consists of:

  • Approximately 12 sessions
  • Two hours per session
  • Sessions spread over approximately 12 weeks

In addition to teaching, visiting faculty members are expected to participate actively in the research activities of the research entity that hosts them.

They are also expected to deliver at least one academic lecture or seminar presentation during their stay.

This means applicants should be prepared to contribute their expertise to students and fellow researchers while also advancing their own academic work.

Key Benefits of the Sciences Po Visiting Faculty Opportunity

The programme offers several benefits that can contribute to an academic’s research, teaching, and professional development.

1. Spend a Semester at Sciences Po in Paris

Selected academics can spend a semester at Sciences Po, giving them the opportunity to experience the academic environment of one of France’s internationally recognised institutions.

Living and working in Paris can also provide researchers with access to a wider European academic environment and opportunities to interact with scholars and institutions beyond their immediate research networks.

2. Join an International Academic Community

Sciences Po welcomes researchers and professors from around the world.

Visiting academics can therefore become part of a diverse academic community where they can exchange ideas with researchers from different countries, disciplines, and research traditions.

International academic exposure can be valuable for scholars seeking to develop collaborative research projects, exchange knowledge, or establish long-term professional relationships.

3. Access the Sciences Po Library

Visiting faculty members have access to the Sciences Po library during their stay.

Access to university research resources can support scholars in conducting literature reviews, developing research projects, preparing publications, and advancing ongoing academic work.

For researchers undertaking projects that require extensive academic resources, library access can be an important component of the visiting experience.

4. Access a Workstation on Campus

Visiting faculty members are provided with access to a workstation on campus.

Having a dedicated workspace can allow visiting academics to conduct research, prepare lectures, write academic papers, meet colleagues, and undertake other scholarly activities during their stay.

5. Teach Students at Sciences Po

Teaching is an important component of the visiting faculty experience.

Visiting professors are generally expected to teach a full course during their semester.

This provides an opportunity to share specialised knowledge and research with students while gaining experience teaching in an international academic environment.

6. Participate in Research Activities

Visiting faculty members are fully integrated into the research activities of the research entity hosting them.

This can provide opportunities to:

  • Attend research seminars
  • Exchange ideas with researchers
  • Discuss ongoing research
  • Explore potential collaborations
  • Present research findings
  • Receive academic feedback
  • Develop new research perspectives

7. Deliver an Academic Lecture or Seminar

Visiting faculty members are expected to deliver at least one academic lecture or seminar presentation during their stay.

This provides an opportunity to showcase their research and expertise to the wider Sciences Po academic community.

Researchers can use such presentations to introduce ongoing projects, share findings, discuss emerging research questions, or contribute to scholarly debates.

8. Develop International Academic Collaborations

International networking is another important potential benefit.

Researchers can interact with professors, academics, doctoral researchers, students, and other members of the Sciences Po research community.

These interactions may create opportunities for future collaboration, joint research, academic publications, conferences, and other scholarly initiatives.

Global Visiting Faculty Program

One of the most accessible opportunities listed on the Sciences Po Visiting Faculty page is the Global Visiting Faculty Program.

The programme is open to outstanding candidates from all disciplines and all continents who wish to spend one semester at Sciences Po.

Its broad geographic eligibility makes it particularly relevant to academics outside France who are interested in international research and teaching experience.

The programme can be of interest to researchers and professors from Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Oceania, and other regions, provided they meet the detailed requirements of the official call.

Key details

  • Academic year: 2027–2028
  • Duration: One semester
  • Disciplines: All disciplines
  • Geographic scope: All continents
  • Target group: Outstanding academics
  • Application deadline: 15 November 2026

Applicants should consult the full call for applications for the complete eligibility and application requirements.

Sciences Po Paris Visiting Fellowship

Another opportunity listed by Sciences Po is the Sciences Po Paris Visiting Fellowship.

This opportunity is designed for outstanding candidates from all disciplines who are currently affiliated with American universities.

The fellowship provides an opportunity for eligible academics to spend one semester at Sciences Po and participate in its academic and research environment.

Because the programme has a specific institutional requirement, academics should confirm their current university affiliation before applying.

Key details

  • Academic year: 2027–2028
  • Duration: One semester
  • Disciplines: All disciplines
  • Institutional requirement: Current affiliation with an American university
  • Application deadline: 15 November 2026

Visiting Faculty: AI & Society

Sciences Po also lists a specialised Visiting Faculty: AI & Society opportunity as part of the TIERED project.

The programme is relevant to academics whose research and expertise relate to artificial intelligence and its relationship with society.

Artificial intelligence is increasingly influencing areas such as:

  • Public policy
  • Governance
  • Democracy
  • Employment
  • Education
  • Law
  • Ethics
  • Economics
  • Technology
  • Social development

Researchers working in these or related fields should review the specific AI & Society call carefully to determine whether their academic profile and research interests match the requirements.

Key detail

The listed application deadline for the 2027–2028 call is 15 November 2026.

Alfred Grosser Chair

The Alfred Grosser Chair is another visiting faculty opportunity listed by Sciences Po.

Unlike the Global Visiting Faculty Program, this opportunity has specific eligibility requirements.

The call is open to professors of social sciences currently affiliated with German universities.

The programme is therefore particularly relevant to academics working in social sciences who are currently based at eligible German universities.

Sciences Po states that the Alfred Grosser Chair is recruiting two visiting professors/researchers.

Key details

  • Target group: Professors of social sciences
  • Institutional affiliation: German universities
  • Academic period: 2027–2028
  • Number of positions: Two visiting professors/researchers
  • Application deadline: 15 November 2026

Other Visiting Faculty and Research Opportunities

The Sciences Po Visiting Faculty page also lists other recurring programmes.

These include the Programme d’échange enseignants-chercheurs – Université Luiss / Sciences Po and the LIEPP International Scholars in Policy Evaluation Programme – Research Stay.

However, the deadlines displayed for these particular calls are earlier in 2026.

The Luiss / Sciences Po faculty exchange was listed with a deadline of 26 June 2026, while the LIEPP International Scholars in Policy Evaluation Programme was listed with a deadline of 7 September 2026.

Applicants should therefore note that these deadlines have passed and should monitor the respective programmes for future application rounds.

Important: Eligibility Varies by Programme

Applicants should not assume that meeting the general description of a Sciences Po visiting faculty member automatically makes them eligible for every programme.

The university clearly indicates that some calls are open to academics from all disciplines and continents, while others are restricted to specific partner universities or regions.

For example:

Programme General eligibility
Global Visiting Faculty Program Outstanding candidates from all disciplines and all continents
Sciences Po Paris Visiting Fellowship Outstanding candidates from all disciplines affiliated with American universities
AI & Society Visiting Faculty Candidates meeting the specific requirements of the AI & Society/TIERED call
Alfred Grosser Chair Social sciences professors affiliated with German universities
Luiss / Sciences Po Exchange Candidates meeting the requirements of the specific institutional exchange
LIEPP International Scholars Programme Candidates meeting the requirements of the specific LIEPP research-stay call

Applicants should always refer to the individual call for the programme they wish to pursue.

What Should Applicants Prepare?

Academics interested in these opportunities should begin preparing well before the deadline.

A strong application should clearly demonstrate the applicant’s academic profile, research experience, teaching expertise, and the value they would bring to the Sciences Po community.

Applicants should consider the following areas.

APPLY HERE

Academic Background

Clearly present your academic qualifications, current position, research area, and professional experience.

Your academic background should demonstrate that you have the expertise required for the particular visiting programme.

Research Experience

Explain your current and previous research work and highlight projects that are relevant to the research community you hope to join at Sciences Po.

Where appropriate, applicants should highlight:

  • Research projects
  • Publications
  • Research findings
  • Academic collaborations
  • Conferences
  • Research grants
  • Policy research
  • Other relevant scholarly contributions

Teaching Experience

Because visiting professors are expected to teach a full course, applicants should demonstrate relevant teaching experience.

Explain the subjects or courses you have taught and identify areas where your expertise could contribute to Sciences Po’s academic programmes.

Proposed Research

Applicants should have a clear idea of what they intend to work on during their stay.

A strong research proposal should communicate:

  1. The research question.
  2. Why the topic is important.
  3. The current state of the research.
  4. The methodology or approach.
  5. The expected contribution.
  6. Why Sciences Po is an appropriate environment for the project.

Contribution to Sciences Po

Applicants should also think about what they can contribute to the university.

This could include:

  • Teaching specialised courses
  • Sharing research expertise
  • Participating in seminars
  • Collaborating with researchers
  • Presenting research findings
  • Developing joint research projects
  • Contributing to interdisciplinary discussions

Why African Researchers Should Pay Attention to the Global Visiting Faculty Program

The Global Visiting Faculty Program is particularly notable for academics from Africa because the call states that it is open to outstanding candidates from all disciplines and all continents.

This potentially creates an opportunity for qualified researchers and professors from African countries to gain international academic experience at Sciences Po.

For African academics, international visiting appointments can contribute to:

  • International research exposure
  • Academic networking
  • Knowledge exchange
  • Research collaboration
  • Teaching experience
  • Professional visibility
  • Development of international partnerships

However, applicants should still review the full official call because being from an eligible continent does not, by itself, guarantee eligibility or selection.

Financial Conditions

The general Sciences Po Visiting Faculty page notes that financial conditions may vary from one programme to another.

This is an important point for prospective applicants.

Applicants should not assume that all visiting faculty programmes offer the same level of financial support.

Before applying, candidates should check the specific call for information concerning:

  • Financial support
  • Travel arrangements
  • Accommodation
  • Stipends or allowances
  • Other programme-related costs
  • Any additional financial requirements

The official individual call should be treated as the primary source for programme-specific financial information.

Application Deadline

Several of the current 2027–2028 Sciences Po Visiting Faculty opportunities have an application deadline of:

15 November 2026

Applicants should avoid waiting until the final day to begin preparing their applications.

Academic applications can require substantial preparation, particularly where candidates need to develop research proposals, teaching plans, academic CVs, publications lists, recommendation materials, or other supporting documents.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should first identify the Sciences Po visiting faculty or fellowship programme that best matches their academic background and institutional affiliation.

Applicants should then review the specific call for applications and follow the instructions provided by Sciences Po.

The official Visiting Faculty page provides access to the individual calls and further information about the different programmes.

Application information:

Frequently Asked Questions

For more information, CLICK HERE

What are the Sciences Po Visiting Faculty Opportunities?

They are opportunities for researchers and professors to spend time at Sciences Po conducting research, teaching, participating in research activities, and engaging with the university’s academic community.

How long is the visiting period?

Several of the listed opportunities involve a one-semester stay at Sciences Po.

Can academics from Africa apply?

Yes, the Global Visiting Faculty Program is open to outstanding candidates from all disciplines and all continents. African academics can therefore potentially apply if they meet the programme’s full requirements.

Can Kenyan researchers apply?

Potentially, particularly through the Global Visiting Faculty Program, which is open to candidates from all continents. Applicants must nevertheless meet the specific requirements of the official call.

Can students apply?

These opportunities are primarily designed for researchers and professors/academic faculty. Applicants should check the individual call to confirm whether their academic career stage meets the requirements.

Do visiting faculty members have to teach?

Yes. Visiting professors are expected to teach one full course, usually consisting of approximately 12 two-hour sessions spread over 12 weeks per semester.

Do visiting faculty members conduct research?

Yes. Visiting faculty members are integrated into the research activities of the research entity hosting them and are expected to contribute actively to the research community.

Do visiting faculty members have to give a lecture?

Yes. Visiting faculty members are expected to deliver at least one academic lecture or seminar presentation during their stay.

What resources can visiting faculty access?

Visiting faculty have access to a workstation on campus, the Sciences Po library, and the university’s research activities and events, particularly those of the research entity hosting them.

Is the opportunity fully funded?

The general page does not state that all visiting faculty programmes are fully funded. Financial terms vary between programmes, so applicants should consult the specific call for details.

What is the deadline?

For several of the 2027–2028 calls currently listed, the application deadline is 15 November 2026.

Conclusion

The Sciences Po Visiting Faculty Opportunities 2027–2028 offer researchers and professors an opportunity to combine international academic experience with teaching, research, networking, and scholarly engagement in Paris.

The opportunities are diverse, with some programmes welcoming outstanding candidates from all disciplines and all continents, while others are designed for academics with specific institutional affiliations or disciplinary backgrounds.

The Global Visiting Faculty Program is particularly noteworthy for international academics because of its broad geographic and disciplinary eligibility. Meanwhile, the Sciences Po Paris Visiting Fellowship, AI & Society Visiting Faculty opportunity, and Alfred Grosser Chair provide more specialised pathways for eligible academics.

Successful visiting faculty members can benefit from access to Sciences Po’s library and campus facilities, participation in research activities, teaching opportunities, academic presentations, and interaction with an international community of researchers and professors.

Academics interested in applying should carefully examine the individual call that matches their profile, prepare their academic and research materials early, and confirm all programme-specific requirements and financial conditions.

For the relevant 2027–2028 calls, the key application deadline is 15 November 2026. Researchers and professors who meet the requirements should use the available time to develop a strong application demonstrating their academic achievements, research interests, teaching experience, and potential contribution to the Sciences Po academic community.

item.content:encoded:
The National Press Foundation (NPF) is inviting professional journalists from around the world to apply for the 2026 Rare Disease Reporting Fellowship and Grants, a fully online journalism training opportunity focused on rare diseases, biotechnology, healthcare access, medical research, and the experiences of patients and families living with rare conditions.

Supported by Fondation Ipsen, the fellowship will provide selected journalists with five days of free online training featuring expert briefings, question-and-answer sessions, and discussions on emerging developments in rare disease research and reporting.

In addition to the training, up to 20 participating journalists may receive reporting grants of up to $2,000 each to support the development of a rare disease reporting project.

Application Deadline: October 22, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET

About the 2026 Rare Disease Reporting Fellowship

Rare diseases affect an estimated 300 million people worldwide, with more than 7,000 confirmed rare diseases. Although advances in biotechnology, medical research, genetic testing, and drug development are creating new possibilities for diagnosis and treatment, people living with rare diseases and their families continue to face substantial challenges.

These challenges can include limited awareness, delayed diagnosis, inadequate healthcare infrastructure, insufficient specialist knowledge, limited treatment options, and difficulties accessing appropriate care.

The 2026 Rare Disease Reporting Fellowship is designed to help journalists develop a stronger understanding of these issues and produce journalism that increases public awareness of rare diseases and the realities faced by patients and their families.

The program is the fifth journalism fellowship in the series supported by Fondation Ipsen.

What Will the Fellowship Focus On?

The five-day online program will bring together journalists and specialists working across the rare disease field.

Participants will receive access to on-the-record briefings and question-and-answer sessions with leading experts, allowing journalists to explore complex medical and scientific issues and develop a deeper understanding of the subjects they may cover.

Topics are expected to include:

  • Rare disease research on the African continent
  • AI-driven drug development
  • Childhood genetic testing
  • Genetic screening
  • Rare disease diagnosis and detection
  • The importance of more inclusive clinical trials
  • Patient advocacy
  • Global rare disease policy and healthcare challenges
  • The experiences of people living with rare diseases
  • The challenges faced by families and caregivers
  • Biotechnology and its potential role in rare disease treatment
  • Healthcare infrastructure and access to care
  • The role of journalism in increasing visibility and understanding of rare diseases

The fellowship will also provide opportunities to hear from leaders of global patient advocacy organizations and experienced journalists covering rare diseases.

This combination of scientific expertise, patient perspectives, advocacy experience, and journalism expertise is intended to give participants a broad foundation for reporting on rare disease issues.

Free Online Journalism Training

All accepted fellows will participate in the online training program at no cost.

The training will take place:

November 16–20, 2026

Sessions will run from:

8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. Eastern Time each day

Because the fellowship requires substantial participation throughout the five-day program, attendance at all sessions is mandatory.

Applicants should therefore make sure they can commit to the entire training schedule before applying.

Reporting Grants of Up to $2,000

One of the additional opportunities offered through the program is financial support for selected fellows who qualify for a reporting grant.

The National Press Foundation will provide up to $2,000 in reporting grants to 20 journalists.

The grants are intended to help journalists undertake a rare disease reporting project of their choice, including expenses related to travel and the time required to complete the reporting.

How the $2,000 Grant Is Paid

The grant is divided into two payments:

  1. $1,000 after completion of the fellowship training
  2. $1,000 after submission of the completed reporting work

The reporting project must be published no later than March 1, 2027.

It is important to note that not every fellow necessarily receives a reporting grant. The fellowship itself is available to accepted participants, while the reporting grants are for fellows who require and qualify for the additional financial support.

Publication Opportunity for Grant Recipients

Journalists who receive a reporting grant will first publish their completed work through their chosen media outlets.

Following publication, their work will also be reprinted in a compilation book produced by Fondation Ipsen, a Paris-based nonprofit organization focused on rare diseases, detection, inclusion, and disability.

The program therefore provides participants with not only training and potential financial support, but also an opportunity for their reporting to contribute to a broader international collection of journalism about rare diseases.

The organizers also provide access to the compilation of work produced by the 2023 NPF fellows, allowing prospective applicants to see examples of reporting from previous participants.

Who Can Apply?

The fellowship is specifically designed for professional journalists.

Eligible journalists may work in different forms of media, including:

  • Print journalism
  • Broadcast journalism
  • Online journalism
  • Digital media
  • Social media journalism
  • Other professional journalism formats

The opportunity is international and is open to professional journalists based in any country.

There is no stated restriction to a particular continent or nationality. Therefore, journalists from Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Oceania, and other regions may apply, provided they meet the program’s professional and language requirements.

The opportunity is not described as being restricted according to race or ethnicity. Applicants from all racial and ethnic backgrounds may apply if they satisfy the eligibility requirements.

English-Language Requirement

Although journalists may work in any language, applicants must have fluency in English.

This requirement is important because the fellowship’s training sessions will be conducted in English.

Applicants should therefore be able to comfortably follow expert presentations, participate in question-and-answer sessions, and engage with the training content in English.

Requirements for Employed Journalists

Journalists who are currently employed must provide a letter of support from their editor as part of their application.

The editor’s letter must include a commitment to allow the journalist to be away from their regular work for four hours each day from November 16–20, 2026.

This requirement exists because full participation in the fellowship sessions is mandatory.

Applicants who are working full-time or on a newsroom schedule should therefore discuss the fellowship with their editor before applying and ensure that the required time can be accommodated.

Requirements for Freelance Journalists

Freelance journalists can also apply.

Instead of an employer’s letter, freelancers should provide a letter from an editor indicating an interest in publishing their work on the rare disease topic.

This means freelance applicants should ideally identify an editor or publication that could potentially publish their proposed reporting.

The letter provides evidence that there is editorial interest in the journalist’s planned work.

Important Dates

Applicants should pay close attention to the following dates:

Important Information Date/Time
Application deadline October 22, 2026
Application closing time 11:59 p.m. ET
Online training November 16–20, 2026
Daily training hours 8:00 a.m.–12:00 p.m. ET
Reporting deadline for grant recipients March 1, 2027

Applicants should not wait until the final hours to submit their applications, particularly if they need to obtain an editor’s letter.

What Makes This Fellowship Relevant to Global Health Journalism?

Rare diseases are often underrepresented in mainstream health reporting despite affecting millions of people globally.

Journalists play an important role in explaining complex medical developments to the public and bringing attention to the experiences of patients and families.

The fellowship’s subject areas connect several rapidly developing areas of health journalism, including biotechnology, artificial intelligence, genetics, drug development, clinical research, healthcare access, and patient advocacy.

The program also specifically includes discussion of rare disease research in Africa, making the training relevant to journalists interested in healthcare and medical research across the African continent.

For journalists working in countries where rare disease awareness, diagnostic infrastructure, specialist services, or access to treatment remain significant challenges, the fellowship may provide additional knowledge and reporting resources for investigating these issues.

Potential Reporting Areas

Participants who receive reporting support will be able to develop a rare disease project of their choosing.

Depending on their interests and the needs of their communities, potential reporting directions could include:

  • Patient experiences and access to diagnosis
  • Rare disease treatment availability
  • Healthcare infrastructure
  • Genetic testing and screening
  • The development of new treatments
  • Biotechnology and rare disease research
  • AI and pharmaceutical research
  • Clinical trial representation and inclusion
  • Rare diseases in African healthcare systems
  • Patient advocacy organizations
  • The financial and social impact of rare diseases on families
  • Caregiving and family experiences
  • Disability and inclusion
  • Public awareness of rare diseases
  • Gaps in national healthcare policies
  • The experiences of underserved rare disease populations

These are examples of possible areas of reporting rather than prescribed project topics. Fellows receiving grants will develop a project of their own choosing.

About the National Press Foundation

The National Press Foundation (NPF) is organizing the fellowship as part of its journalism training and reporting initiatives.

The organization is providing the training to help journalists better understand complex issues and produce informed reporting on rare diseases.

The 2026 program represents the fifth fellowship in this rare disease journalism series.

Support from Fondation Ipsen

The fellowship is made possible with support from Fondation Ipsen, a Paris-based nonprofit organization whose work includes rare diseases, detection, inclusion, and disability.

Fondation Ipsen has also supported the publication of previous reporting from the program.

The previous compilation of work by 2023 NPF fellows is available through the foundation, providing an example of how participating journalists’ reporting can contribute to broader international discussions about rare diseases.

Why Journalists Should Pay Attention to the Application Requirements

Although the fellowship is free, applicants should carefully review the participation requirements before submitting an application.

The most important considerations are:

  1. Professional journalism status: The opportunity is intended for professional journalists.
  2. International eligibility: Journalists can be based in any country.
  3. English fluency: Applicants must be fluent in English because the training is conducted in English.
  4. Full participation: Attendance at all training sessions is mandatory.
  5. Time commitment: Sessions take place for four hours each day from November 16–20.
  6. Editor support: Employed journalists need an editor’s letter confirming they can participate.
  7. Freelance applicants: Freelancers need an editor’s letter demonstrating interest in publishing their work.
  8. Reporting grant: Up to 20 journalists may receive grants of up to $2,000.
  9. Reporting deadline: Grant-supported work must be submitted and published by March 1, 2027.
  10. Application deadline: Applications must be submitted by 11:59 p.m. ET on October 22, 2026.

How to Apply

Interested professional journalists should complete the official online application before the deadline.

Application Deadline: October 22, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET

Applicants should ensure that all required information and supporting documentation are prepared before submitting the application.

Employed journalists should arrange their editor’s support letter, while freelance journalists should secure a letter from an editor who has expressed interest in publishing their proposed reporting.

Key Takeaways

The 2026 Rare Disease Reporting Fellowship and Grants offers professional journalists an opportunity to receive specialized training on some of the most important developments and challenges surrounding rare diseases.

Selected fellows will participate in a free five-day online program covering topics ranging from African rare disease research and genetic screening to AI-driven drug development and inclusive clinical trials.

In addition, up to 20 journalists may receive reporting grants of up to $2,000, divided into two $1,000 payments. Grant recipients will use the support to develop rare disease reporting projects, with completed work required to be published by March 1, 2027.

The program is open internationally, but applicants must be professional journalists with English fluency and must be able to attend all required sessions. The specific documentation required will depend on whether an applicant is employed or working as a freelancer.

Click HERE to read more and apply.

Conclusion

The 2026 Rare Disease Reporting Fellowship and Grants is designed to strengthen journalists’ ability to report on rare diseases, medical research, biotechnology, patient experiences, and healthcare access. Through expert-led online training, access to patient advocacy perspectives, and potential reporting grants, the program provides participating journalists with resources to develop informed and impactful rare disease coverage.

Professional journalists from any country who meet the eligibility requirements and can commit to the full five-day training should take note of the October 22, 2026, application deadline. Those seeking reporting support should also consider the additional requirements surrounding editor support, grant eligibility, and publication of the resulting work by March 1, 2027.

Click HERE for more fellowship opportunities.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the NHS Graduate Management Training Scheme (GMTS) 2027 entry, offering graduates and eligible applicants an opportunity to develop their leadership, management and professional skills while working within the National Health Service.

The NHS GMTS is designed for people who demonstrate passion, potential and leadership capability. According to the programme, its recruitment process is not focused simply on what applicants studied, which university they attended, or what previous work experience they have. Instead, the selection process is designed to assess candidates’ strengths and potential to become future NHS leaders.

Applications for 2027 entry are currently open and will close on 28 October at 11:30am.

Apply for the NHS Graduate Management Training Scheme 2027

What Is the NHS Graduate Management Training Scheme?

The NHS Graduate Management Training Scheme (GMTS) is a structured graduate development and employment programme designed to develop future leaders within the NHS.

The Scheme combines employment, professional development, academic study and practical experience. Successful applicants become full-time NHS employees rather than students on a conventional university programme. The official eligibility information states that trainees undertake at least two years of work experience, professional leadership training and academic qualifications.

The programme is intended for individuals who want to build a career in healthcare management and leadership and who are interested in contributing to the delivery and improvement of health and care services.

The NHS currently lists a starting salary of £31,276, with the possibility of an increase to £33,681 after 12 months, alongside NHS employment benefits.

Why Consider the NHS Graduate Management Training Scheme?

The GMTS provides an opportunity to develop professional skills while gaining practical experience within the NHS.

Depending on the specialism, trainees can develop experience in areas such as:

  • General management
  • Human resources
  • Finance
  • Digital and health informatics
  • Engineering and estates management

The exact academic qualification, duration and entry requirements can vary by specialism. For example, the HR pathway is listed as a two-year programme for applicants with any degree at 2:2 or above.

The Scheme also provides structured support throughout the trainee journey, including programme management, placement support, educational support and access to experienced colleagues and previous trainees.

NHS GMTS 2027 Recruitment Process

The 2027 recruitment process consists of several stages. Applicants should be prepared to complete online assessments before progressing to the Virtual Assessment Centre.

Registration and Application Form

The first step is to register and complete the online application form.

Applicants should ensure that they meet the relevant entry requirements before beginning the application process.

The NHS specifically encourages applicants to apply early because successful candidates will need time to complete the assessment stages that follow the application.

Stage 1: Future Potential Assessment

The first assessment stage is the Future Potential Assessment, which takes place online.

The assessment is expected to take approximately 45 minutes, although it is not time limited.

This stage is designed to help applicants learn more about the type of work they could undertake on the Scheme while allowing the NHS to assess aspects of their potential.

Before beginning the actual assessment, applicants will have the opportunity to practise each type of question.

One important feature of the process is that all candidates receive a feedback report after completing this stage, providing information about their performance.

If successful, applicants are invited to proceed to Stage 2.

Stage 2: NHS GMTS Alignment Assessment

Successful Stage 1 candidates can move on to the NHS GMTS Alignment Assessment.

This assessment takes approximately 60 minutes.

One of its main features is the inclusion of video responses, allowing candidates to demonstrate more about themselves as individuals.

Applicants will have the opportunity to practise each question type before completing the assessment. Although the overall assessment takes approximately one hour, only the video-based questions are timed.

Candidates also receive a feedback report after completing Stage 2.

Human Review of Video Responses

An important point for applicants is that the NHS GMTS states that its team manually reviews video interview responses and does not use artificial intelligence for this part of the process.

Candidates should therefore focus on presenting their own experiences, motivations and examples clearly and authentically.

Successful candidates proceed to the Virtual Assessment Centre.

Stage 3: Virtual Assessment Centre

The Virtual Assessment Centre (VAC) represents the final assessment stage of the recruitment process.

VACs for the 2027 entry process are scheduled to begin in January 2027 and continue through February 2027.

The VAC is a half-day assessment involving several exercises.

During the assessment, candidates will have the opportunity to:

  • Complete a range of assessment exercises
  • Meet members of the NHS team
  • Interact with other candidates
  • Demonstrate their strengths in different situations
  • Experience the assessment environment virtually

The NHS encourages applicants to be themselves throughout the process.

Candidates receive a feedback report after the VAC regardless of the outcome.

Possible VAC Outcomes

Following the Virtual Assessment Centre, candidates can receive one of three outcomes:

  1. Successful at VAC – an immediate offer will be made.
  2. Reserve list – the candidate may be contacted if a place on the Scheme becomes available.
  3. Unsuccessful at VAC – the candidate will not progress to an offer.

The VAC is the final assessment stage. Placement allocation happens afterwards and is separate from the assessment process.

Placement Allocation

Candidates who successfully pass the VAC and receive an offer then enter the allocation process.

Allocation involves matching successful candidates with available placements within NHS organisations.

The NHS considers factors including:

  • Assessment scores
  • Candidate preferences
  • Available placement roles
  • Regional considerations
  • Personal circumstances where applicable

The NHS states that it will endeavour to match individuals with the closest possible placement based on their indicated preferences. However, a preferred region cannot necessarily be guaranteed because placement availability and other factors affect the allocation process.

This means applicants should consider flexibility when thinking about potential placement locations.

Offer and Onboarding

Candidates who successfully pass the VAC and are matched with a placement will receive an offer to join the Scheme.

The next stage involves:

  • Pre-employment checks
  • Qualification verification
  • Immigration/right-to-work checks where applicable
  • Onboarding
  • Preparation for employment

Successful candidates are expected to be ready to join the Scheme on the first Monday of September 2027.

Preparation Materials for Applicants

The NHS GMTS provides preparation resources throughout the assessment process.

Once an applicant applies, relevant preparation materials become available in their account at each stage.

For Stage 1 and Stage 2, applicants can access:

  • Hints and tips videos
  • Practice tests
  • Examples similar to the actual assessments
  • Opportunities to practise question types

For the Virtual Assessment Centre, preparation support includes:

  • Coaching calls
  • Hints and tips
  • Platform familiarisation videos

Applicants are not required to complete all preparation materials. However, the NHS encourages candidates to use them because they can help applicants become familiar with the assessment process.

The online practice assessments can also be used to test equipment and internet connections before completing the actual assessments.

The VAC platform has its own technical-check function, allowing candidates to check that their microphone and camera are working correctly.

Reasonable Adjustments During the Recruitment Process

The NHS GMTS recognises that applicants may require reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process.

Applicants are encouraged to disclose their adjustment needs if they require additional support.

The programme states that disclosure is a personal decision and that applicants do not need to provide information they prefer to keep private. The recruitment team only needs sufficient information to understand what adjustments are required.

The VAC team may also ask whether there are medical conditions that need to be considered in order to provide appropriate support.

The stated objective is to ensure that candidates can participate in the selection process comfortably and fairly.

Fair and Inclusive Assessment

The NHS GMTS states that assessors receive training designed to support a fair and inclusive recruitment process.

This training includes recognising and avoiding unconscious bias.

The programme describes its approach as being committed to an equitable assessment experience for candidates.

The NHS’s eligibility information also states its commitment to equality of opportunity and says that candidates should not receive less favourable treatment on grounds including age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, or sexual orientation.

NHS Graduate Management Training Scheme Entry Requirements

Applicants should carefully check the requirements for their preferred specialism because requirements differ for some pathways.

For General Management, Human Resources, Finance and Digital – Health Informatics, the standard minimum requirement is a 2:2 degree in any subject.

The NHS also recognises certain alternative qualifications, including:

  • A postgraduate qualification such as an MBA, Master’s or PhD
  • Certain health- or management-related degree-level equivalent qualifications
  • NVQ Level 5 in Management
  • Diploma in Management Studies
  • Diploma in Nursing, Midwifery or Health Visiting
  • Diploma from the Chartered Society of Physiotherapy
  • Diploma in Speech and Language Therapy
  • Diploma from the College of Occupational Therapy
  • Diploma from the College of Radiographers
  • Diploma in Social Work or Certificate of Qualification in Social Work

Certain qualifications are specifically listed as not acceptable, including a Certificate in Management Studies, general DipHE qualifications outside the accepted list, ONC/OND, HNC/HND, CGLI/C&G and certain operating department certificates or diplomas.

Engineering and Estates Management Requirements

The Engineering and Estates Management (EEM) pathway has different academic requirements.

Applicants need at least a 2:2 degree in an appropriate engineering discipline, including:

  • Mechanical Engineering
  • Electrical Engineering
  • Building Services Engineering

The degree must be accredited by the Engineering Council for the relevant standard route to professional chartership.

The NHS also notes that applicants holding an MEng, whether through a BEng plus Master’s or a structured four-year MEng, are not eligible for the Estates Engineering Management specialism.

Right to Work in the United Kingdom

One of the most important requirements for applicants is the right to work in the UK.

All candidates must have the right to work in the UK for the entire duration of the Scheme.

The NHS GMTS is a full-time employment programme rather than a student programme. Applicants are responsible for ensuring that they have the appropriate immigration status or visa to work in the UK for the complete duration of the Scheme.

If an applicant does not have the required right to work, their application or offer may be withdrawn.

Offers are subject to pre-employment checks, which can include:

  • Immigration status verification
  • Qualification verification
  • Recent proof of address in the UK
  • Other employment checks

The NHS notes that immigration requirements can change and that applicants should ensure their status allows them to undertake the full programme.

Is Previous Work Experience Required?

The NHS GMTS does not require specific work experience as an eligibility condition.

This is important because the Scheme’s recruitment approach focuses on potential rather than simply selecting applicants based on their previous employment history.

However, the NHS states that tangible examples of work experience, whether paid or unpaid, can be useful during the interview and assessment process.

Examples could include volunteering or other activities that demonstrate skills, initiative, teamwork, leadership, communication or an understanding of healthcare.

For example, the NHS notes that volunteering at a local hospital can provide useful experience and help an applicant better understand the challenges facing NHS services.

Can Current NHS Employees Apply?

Yes.

The NHS Graduate Management Training Scheme is open to current NHS employees, who are referred to as “in-service” trainees.

Current NHS staff must still meet the same academic eligibility and right-to-work requirements as other applicants. There are no academic eligibility exceptions simply because someone already works for the NHS.

The recruitment and assessment process is also the same for current NHS employees and external applicants.

Current NHS employees who are successful may have their previous reckonable NHS service considered as part of the employment process.

Final-Year Students Can Apply

Students who have just started their final year of a degree can apply, provided they meet the relevant requirements.

The NHS states that final-year students must have obtained their final confirmed degree classification, with a minimum of 2:2, by mid-August 2027.

Successful candidates then join the Scheme on the first Monday of September 2027.

This makes the 2027 intake relevant to students who are currently approaching the final stage of their undergraduate studies as well as graduates who already hold their qualifications.

No Age Limit

There is no age limit for applying to the NHS Graduate Management Training Scheme.

The NHS states that applicants who meet the minimum entry requirements, have an interest in health and care, and consider the GMTS an appropriate career move are welcome to apply.

What Happens After Completing the Scheme?

During the Scheme, trainees are employed on a fixed-term contract.

The NHS states that trainees undertake work experience, professional leadership training and academic qualifications. Depending on the specialism, the employment period can be 24 or 30 months.

The Scheme is intended to support participants in progressing into NHS careers after completing their training.

The NHS reports that the average salary earned by trainees in their first NHS role after completing the Scheme is around £44,000, although actual salaries vary according to the role obtained.

The programme does not guarantee a particular job after completion, but the NHS GMTS provides support with finding a first substantive NHS position, including job-search advice through its support network.

Salary and Benefits

The current NHS GMTS information lists a minimum starting salary of £31,276, with a potential increase after 12 months. Depending on placement location, a High Cost Area Supplement may also apply.

Other benefits include access to the NHS Pension Scheme and employee support programmes.

The Scheme’s published information also highlights benefits such as:

  • NHS Pension Scheme
  • Employee Assistance Programme
  • Cycle2Work scheme
  • Employment within the NHS
  • Structured professional development
  • Academic study
  • Leadership training
  • Placement experience
  • Support from programme and placement teams

Current NHS employees may have different salary arrangements depending on their existing NHS employment and recognised service.

Key Features of the NHS GMTS 2027 Opportunity

For applicants considering the programme, the main features include:

  • 2027 entry to the NHS Graduate Management Training Scheme
  • Applications currently open
  • Minimum 2:2 degree for most specialisms
  • Degree can be in any subject for General Management, HR, Finance and Digital – Health Informatics
  • Separate engineering degree requirements for Engineering and Estates Management
  • No specific previous work experience required
  • No age limit
  • Current NHS employees can apply
  • Final-year students can apply if they meet the qualification deadline
  • Full-time employment during the Scheme
  • Professional leadership development
  • Academic qualifications
  • Practical NHS work experience
  • Online assessments
  • Virtual Assessment Centre
  • Placement allocation following successful assessment
  • Structured preparation materials
  • Feedback following assessment stages
  • Reasonable adjustment support
  • Trained assessors
  • UK right-to-work requirement

NHS GMTS 2027 Application Timeline

Applicants should be aware of the key dates and stages associated with the 2027 intake.

Application deadline

28 October 2026 at 11:30am

Stage 1

Future Potential Assessment completed online following successful registration and application.

Stage 2

Successful Stage 1 candidates proceed to the NHS GMTS Alignment Assessment, including video responses.

January–February 2027

Virtual Assessment Centres are scheduled to take place.

September 2027

Successful candidates who complete the assessment, placement matching and onboarding process are expected to begin the Scheme on the first Monday of September 2027.

How to Apply for the NHS Graduate Management Training Scheme 2027

Applicants should first review the eligibility requirements for the specialism they wish to pursue.

Step 1: Check eligibility

Confirm that you have:

  • The required academic qualification
  • The appropriate qualification for your chosen specialism
  • The right to work in the UK for the entire Scheme
  • Any additional requirements relevant to your pathway

Step 2: Complete the application

Applications are submitted through the NHS GMTS application system.

NHS GMTS 2027 Application Portal

Step 3: Complete Stage 1

If your application progresses, complete the Future Potential Assessment.

Use the available practice materials to familiarise yourself with the question formats.

Step 4: Complete Stage 2

Successful Stage 1 applicants move to the NHS GMTS Alignment Assessment, including video responses.

Step 5: Attend the Virtual Assessment Centre

Candidates who successfully pass the online assessment stages are invited to the half-day VAC.

Step 6: Placement allocation

Successful candidates are matched with available NHS placements according to the Scheme’s allocation process.

Step 7: Pre-employment checks and onboarding

Candidates who are successfully matched complete the necessary checks and onboarding before joining the Scheme.

Tips for Preparing Your Application

Although the NHS GMTS does not require applicants to have a particular academic subject or specific work history for most pathways, applicants should still prepare carefully.

1. Understand the pathway you are applying for

Read the requirements for your chosen specialism carefully. The standard requirements do not apply identically to every pathway, particularly Engineering and Estates Management.

2. Use the official practice materials

The Scheme provides practice assessments, hints and tips videos and technical checks. These resources can help applicants understand what to expect.

3. Prepare examples from your experience

Think about situations where you have demonstrated qualities such as:

  • Leadership
  • Teamwork
  • Communication
  • Problem-solving
  • Adaptability
  • Initiative
  • Resilience
  • Working with others
  • Responding to change

These examples do not necessarily have to come from formal employment.

4. Prepare for video responses

Because Stage 2 includes video questions, applicants should become comfortable explaining their experiences and motivations clearly on camera.

5. Check your technology

Make sure your:

  • Camera works
  • Microphone works
  • Internet connection is reliable
  • Computer is suitable for the assessment platform
  • Assessment environment is appropriate

The NHS provides technical checks as part of its preparation process.

6. Apply early

Although the final deadline is 28 October at 11:30am, applicants are encouraged to apply early because there are multiple assessment stages after the initial application.

Learn more HERE

Frequently Asked Questions

Can final-year students apply?

Yes. Final-year students can apply if they meet the Scheme’s requirements and have their final confirmed degree classification of at least 2:2 by mid-August 2027.

Is a specific degree subject required?

For General Management, Human Resources, Finance and Digital – Health Informatics, the minimum requirement is a 2:2 degree in any subject. Engineering and Estates Management has specific engineering-degree requirements.

Do I need previous work experience?

No specific work experience is required. However, paid or unpaid experience can provide useful examples during the recruitment process.

Can current NHS employees apply?

Yes. Current NHS employees can apply as in-service trainees, but they must meet the same academic and right-to-work requirements.

Is there an age limit?

No. The NHS states that there is no age limit for applicants.

Do I need the right to work in the UK?

Yes. Applicants must have the right to work in the UK for the entire duration of the Scheme.

When does the 2027 Scheme begin?

Successful candidates are expected to join on the first Monday of September 2027.

Does completing the Scheme guarantee a permanent NHS job?

No. Trainees are employed during the Scheme, and the NHS provides support with finding a first substantive NHS role afterwards, but a particular job is not guaranteed.

When is the application deadline?

Applications for 2027 entry close on 28 October 2026 at 11:30am.

Conclusion

The NHS Graduate Management Training Scheme 2027 provides an opportunity for eligible graduates, final-year students and current NHS employees to develop their leadership and management careers while gaining practical experience within the NHS.

The recruitment process places considerable emphasis on potential, strengths, motivation and individual capability, rather than requiring applicants to come from one particular academic discipline or have a specific professional background. For most pathways, a 2:2 degree in any subject is sufficient academically, while Engineering and Estates Management has separate engineering requirements. Applicants must also have the right to work in the UK for the entire duration of the Scheme.

The selection process progresses from the application and Future Potential Assessment through the NHS GMTS Alignment Assessment and finally to the Virtual Assessment Centre. Successful candidates then go through placement allocation, pre-employment checks and onboarding before beginning the Scheme in September 2027.

With applications currently open, prospective applicants should review the requirements for their preferred pathway, make use of the available preparation resources and submit their application before the 28 October 2026 at 11:30am deadline.

item.content:encoded:
The Royal Society Career Development Fellowship 2027 is a four-year postdoctoral research fellowship designed to support talented early-career scientists from underrepresented backgrounds as they establish and develop independent research careers in the United Kingdom.

The fellowship provides substantial research funding, alongside structured mentoring, training, networking and career-development opportunities. The scheme is particularly intended to support researchers from Black heritage backgrounds, including mixed Black backgrounds, during the transition from postgraduate study into the early stages of a postdoctoral research career.

The current fellowship round is open, with applications closing on 18 November 2026. The scheme is intended for researchers whose work falls within the Royal Society’s natural sciences remit, including areas such as biological research and biomedical sciences, chemistry, engineering, mathematics and physics.

About the Royal Society Career Development Fellowship

The Career Development Fellowship (CDF) is a four-year postdoctoral research fellowship created to support the retention and progression of researchers from underrepresented backgrounds within STEM.

The fellowship combines financial support for research with a comprehensive programme of mentoring, training and networking. Its broader purpose is to help award holders establish a successful research career within a UK institution and strengthen their long-term participation in science, technology, engineering and mathematics.

According to the Royal Society, the scheme was developed following cross-sector discussions and research examining trends in the representation of ethnic minority researchers across higher education. This work identified a particular need for support for researchers from Black, Mixed Black African, Black Caribbean and other Black heritage backgrounds, especially those making the transition from postgraduate education into the early postdoctoral stage.

The current programme is being offered as a pilot focused on researchers from Black heritage backgrounds. The Royal Society states that, if the pilot is successful, the programme may subsequently be broadened to other underrepresented groups.

What the Career Development Fellowship Aims to Achieve

The Royal Society Career Development Fellowship is structured around several objectives:

  • Supporting talented early-career researchers from underrepresented backgrounds as they take the first steps toward establishing their research in a UK institution.
  • Giving researchers the opportunity to undertake high-quality, curiosity-led research.
  • Providing promising researchers with mentoring, networking, training and other forms of professional support.
  • Helping researchers from underrepresented groups pursue long-term careers in STEM.
  • Contributing to the development and strengthening of the UK scientific workforce.

The Royal Society also highlights the importance of diversity in achieving excellence in STEM. The organisation states that bringing together researchers with different backgrounds, perspectives and experiences can contribute to innovation and creativity in science.

What the Fellowship Offers

Successful applicants can apply for up to £703,800 over four years.

The funding can support several components of the fellowship and research programme, including:

  • Research Fellow salary: A contribution toward the Research Fellow’s salary and associated on-costs at 80%.
  • Directly allocated costs: Funding for eligible directly allocated costs at 80%.
  • Research expenses: Research expenses can be covered at 100%.
  • Relocation and visa costs: Eligible applicants can request relocation and visa costs for themselves and their dependants, including a partner and children, in addition to the £703,800 grant cap over four years.

Beyond the financial award, the fellowship includes a tailored programme of training, mentoring and engagement designed to help researchers strengthen their professional and research careers.

Royal Society Research Fellows can also access additional career-development and engagement opportunities, including training related to leadership, science communication and public engagement, as well as activities coordinated by the Society’s science policy and schools engagement teams.

Flexible Support for Researchers

The fellowship also recognises that researchers may have different personal and professional circumstances.

The Royal Society provides flexibility that can accommodate arrangements such as:

  • Part-time working
  • Sabbaticals
  • Secondments
  • Maternity leave
  • Paternity leave
  • Shared parental leave
  • Adoptive leave
  • Extended sick leave

There is also provision for financial support for childcare costs arising from activities such as attending conferences, collaborative research visits and invited talks.

This means the fellowship is not solely focused on providing research funding; it also incorporates measures intended to support researchers in managing different circumstances while developing their careers.

Who Can Apply?

The Royal Society Career Development Fellowship has specific eligibility requirements. Prospective applicants should carefully review these requirements before beginning an application.

1. Black heritage background

Applicants must self-identify as being from a Black heritage background, including a mixed Black background. The current pilot specifically focuses on researchers from Black heritage backgrounds.

2. UK connection

Applicants must satisfy at least one of the specified UK-connection requirements. You can be eligible if you are:

  • A UK national; or
  • Someone who has completed part of their education in the UK through an undergraduate, Master’s or PhD degree; or
  • Someone who holds or has previously held a postdoctoral researcher position in the UK.

Importantly, applicants do not necessarily have to be UK-domiciled.

The Royal Society states that both UK- and non-UK-domiciled researchers who intend to conduct their research in the UK can apply. Applicants can be of any nationality, provided they satisfy the scheme’s other eligibility requirements.

Researchers who require a visa are also eligible to apply for a Global Talent Visa through the fast-track endorsement process described by the Royal Society.

3. Academic and career stage

Applicants must have a PhD, or be expected to have obtained one by the time the fellowship funding begins.

They must also have less than 24 months of postdoctoral experience. This makes the programme particularly relevant to researchers who are at the early stage of their postdoctoral careers and are seeking to establish themselves as independent researchers.

4. Research discipline

The applicant’s research must fall within the Royal Society’s natural sciences remit.

The eligible areas include, but are not limited to:

  • Biological research
  • Biomedical sciences
  • Chemistry
  • Engineering
  • Mathematics
  • Physics

Applicants should consult the Royal Society’s detailed subject-group information to determine whether their specific research area falls within the fellowship’s supported disciplines.

Nationality and Geographic Eligibility

The fellowship is open to researchers from any nationality, provided they meet the scheme’s eligibility conditions.

Therefore, the opportunity is not restricted exclusively to UK citizens. International researchers can also apply if they have the required UK connection through their education or postdoctoral research experience and intend to carry out their research in the UK.

For example, a researcher from an African country could potentially qualify if they meet the fellowship’s Black heritage requirement, academic and postdoctoral experience requirements, natural sciences research requirements, and one of the specified UK-connection requirements.

Research Focus and Academic Areas

One of the important features of the Career Development Fellowship is its emphasis on high-quality, curiosity-led research.

The fellowship is intended for researchers whose work falls within the Royal Society’s natural sciences remit rather than being restricted to one specific scientific discipline.

This broad remit means that eligible researchers working in fields such as mathematics, physics, engineering, chemistry, biological sciences and biomedical sciences may potentially find the fellowship relevant to their research careers.

Royal Society and Alzheimer’s Society Career Development Fellowship

The scheme also includes a partnership between the Royal Society and Alzheimer’s Society.

Under this partnership, funding is available for an applicant undertaking research that is directly relevant to dementia, excluding clinical and interventional studies on humans.

This provides an additional route within the fellowship for eligible researchers whose research directly addresses dementia-related questions within the stated research restrictions.

Application Timeline for the 2027 Fellowship

Applicants should take note of the key dates for the current round:

Application milestone Date
Applications open 22 September 2026
Application deadline 18 November 2026
Decision by 30 June 2027

The application deadline is therefore 18 November 2026. Applications should be submitted before the closing date through the Royal Society’s grant management system.

How to Apply

Applications are submitted through Flexi-Grant, the Royal Society’s application and grant-management system.

Applicants should ensure that they carefully review the fellowship’s scheme notes and eligibility requirements before submitting an application.

The assessment process is overseen by the Career Development Fellowship panel. Applicants who are shortlisted will be invited to an in-person interview at the Royal Society. During the interview, shortlisted applicants are expected to demonstrate the importance and scientific validity of their proposed research.

The Royal Society also provides application tips to help prospective applicants understand the expectations of the fellowship application.

APPLY HERE

Important Things Applicants Should Prepare

Because this is a competitive postdoctoral research fellowship, prospective applicants should pay close attention to the relationship between their academic background, research proposal and career-development objectives.

Before applying, applicants should ensure that they can clearly demonstrate:

  1. Eligibility for the Black heritage requirement under the current pilot.
  2. A PhD or expected PhD completion by the time funding begins.
  3. Less than 24 months of postdoctoral experience.
  4. A qualifying UK connection through nationality, education or postdoctoral research experience.
  5. Research within the Royal Society’s natural sciences remit.
  6. A clear research direction suitable for the fellowship’s focus on high-quality, curiosity-led research.
  7. A credible pathway toward establishing a successful research career in the UK.

Applicants should also review the official scheme notes because the detailed eligibility, funding and assessment requirements should be treated as the authoritative basis for preparing an application.

Training, Mentoring and Networking Opportunities

An important part of the Career Development Fellowship is that it goes beyond conventional research funding.

Successful fellows receive access to a programme designed to support their wider professional development. This includes mentoring, training and networking opportunities, all intended to help researchers build the skills, professional connections and experience required for a sustainable scientific career.

Additional Royal Society opportunities can include professional development in areas such as:

  • Leadership
  • Science communication
  • Public engagement
  • Research networking
  • Engagement with science policy
  • Engagement with schools and wider audiences

These opportunities are intended to complement the research component of the fellowship and help researchers develop beyond their immediate scientific projects.

Click HERE to sign up to the Information Session.

Funding for Relocation and Visas

International researchers should pay particular attention to the fellowship’s provisions for relocation and immigration-related costs.

The Royal Society states that relocation and visa costs for fellows and their dependants can be requested in addition to the £703,800 four-year grant cap. This can be particularly relevant to researchers who are currently based outside the United Kingdom and intend to relocate for the fellowship.

The Royal Society also states that applicants who require a visa may be eligible for a Global Talent Visa through the fast-track endorsement process.

Fellowship Duration

The Career Development Fellowship lasts for four years.

This provides successful researchers with a substantial period in which to conduct their research, develop their academic profile, establish professional networks and participate in structured career-development activities.

The four-year structure is particularly relevant to the fellowship’s broader objective of helping early-career researchers move toward establishing a sustainable research career within a UK institution.

Why Early-Career Researchers Should Review This Opportunity

The fellowship brings together several components that are relevant to researchers at the early postdoctoral stage.

Rather than providing research funding alone, it combines:

  • Up to £703,800 over four years
  • Support toward the fellow’s salary
  • Funding for eligible research expenses
  • Directly allocated costs
  • Potential relocation and visa support
  • Mentoring
  • Training
  • Networking
  • Leadership and professional development
  • Science communication and public engagement opportunities
  • Flexible arrangements for certain personal circumstances

The programme is specifically designed around the career-development needs of researchers from an underrepresented group in STEM, with the current pilot focused on researchers from Black heritage backgrounds.

Key Facts at a Glance

Opportunity: Royal Society Career Development Fellowship 2027

Provider: The Royal Society

Category: Fellowship

Career stage: Early career/postdoctoral

Duration: Four years

Maximum funding: Up to £703,800

Application opens: 22 September 2026

Deadline: 18 November 2026

Decision by: 30 June 2027

Location: United Kingdom

Research areas: Natural sciences, including biological research and biomedical sciences, chemistry, engineering, mathematics and physics

Target group: Researchers from Black heritage backgrounds, including mixed Black backgrounds

Nationality: Applicants can be of any nationality, subject to the scheme’s UK-connection and other eligibility requirements

Domicile: Both UK- and non-UK-domiciled researchers may be eligible

Application platform: Royal Society Flexi-Grant

Interview: Shortlisted applicants will be invited to an in-person interview at the Royal Society.

Application Deadline

The deadline to apply for the Royal Society Career Development Fellowship 2027 is 18 November 2026.

Applicants should not wait until the final day to begin preparing their applications. Prospective candidates should first confirm that they meet every eligibility requirement, review the official scheme notes, develop their research proposal and prepare the supporting information required through the Royal Society’s Flexi-Grant system.

Visit HERE for more information about the Royal Society Career Development Fellowship 2027.

Conclusion

The Royal Society Career Development Fellowship 2027 provides a four-year funding and professional-development opportunity for eligible early-career researchers from Black heritage backgrounds who are seeking to establish research careers in the United Kingdom.

With funding of up to £703,800, support for research expenses and salary-related costs, potential relocation and visa funding, and access to structured mentoring, training and networking, the fellowship is designed to provide both financial and professional support during an important stage of an academic researcher’s career.

The opportunity is open to applicants of any nationality who satisfy the relevant eligibility conditions, including the required UK connection, PhD and postdoctoral-experience requirements, Black heritage criterion and natural sciences research requirement. Both UK- and non-UK-domiciled researchers intending to conduct their research in the UK can be eligible.

Researchers interested in applying should carefully examine the official scheme requirements and prepare their applications well ahead of the 18 November 2026 deadline.

Official Application and Further Information

Applicants can access the Royal Society’s fellowship information, scheme notes and application system through the official Royal Society resources provided in the source material.

Pro tip: Before submitting your application, carefully check the detailed scheme notes against your nationality or UK connection, PhD completion status, postdoctoral experience, research discipline and Black heritage eligibility. This can help you confirm your eligibility before investing substantial time in the full application.
