item.content:encoded:
Entrepreneurs building businesses designed to create meaningful social, environmental or economic impact can now apply to Halcyon’s founder community through its new year-round open application process. Instead of waiting for a single annual application deadline, eligible ventures can submit an Eligibility Application at any time of the year and have their applications reviewed on a rolling basis.

The new application model is designed to make Halcyon’s founder selection process more accessible, flexible and open throughout the year. Rather than requiring every venture to apply directly to a specific fellowship at a fixed time, Halcyon has introduced a two-step application process that begins with a short eligibility application.

If a venture meets Halcyon’s criteria and a future fellowship is considered a suitable match, the venture may be invited to complete a more detailed Invitational Application.

For entrepreneurs developing solutions with the potential to generate positive impact at scale, this creates a pathway to be considered for future Halcyon fellowship opportunities without having to wait for a particular fellowship application window to open.

What Is the Halcyon Open Application?

The Halcyon Open Application is a year-round entry point for impact-driven ventures interested in becoming part of Halcyon’s founder community.

Under the updated process, entrepreneurs begin by completing a relatively short Eligibility Application. This first stage allows Halcyon to determine whether a venture is potentially suitable for its programmes.

The application asks applicants to provide information about areas such as

  • The venture’s mission
  • The stage of the venture
  • Its impact focus
  • The nature of the solution being developed
  • The venture’s potential fit with Halcyon’s programmes

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, meaning entrepreneurs do not have to wait for one specific annual deadline to submit the first-stage application.

If the venture meets Halcyon’s eligibility criteria, its application can remain relevant for consideration when a fellowship opens that aligns with the venture.

How the New Halcyon Application Process Works

The application process consists of two main stages.

Step 1: Submit the Eligibility Application

The first step is an Eligibility Application, which is open throughout the year.

This initial application is designed to help Halcyon quickly assess whether a venture may be a suitable fit for its programmes.

Applicants will be asked basic questions about their venture, including its:

  1. Mission
  2. Development stage
  3. Impact focus
  4. General approach and solution
  5. Potential fit with Halcyon’s programmes

The first stage is intentionally more accessible than a full fellowship application.

Once submitted, applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.

Important requirement: Apply only once.

Applicants should pay close attention to one important rule.

The Eligibility Application can only be submitted once.

Halcyon states that duplicate applications will be automatically rejected. Entrepreneurs should therefore make sure their first submission is accurate, complete and carefully prepared before submitting it.

This is particularly important because applicants should not treat the eligibility form as a preliminary form that can simply be resubmitted repeatedly with different information.

Step 2: The Invitational Application

The second stage is significantly more detailed and is available by invitation only.

If Halcyon determines that a venture meets its eligibility criteria and a relevant fellowship programme becomes available, the venture may receive an invitation to complete the second-stage application.

The Invitational Application gives Halcyon an opportunity to understand the venture in much greater depth.

Applicants can expect this stage to examine areas such as

  • The founding team
  • The innovation behind the venture
  • The problem being addressed
  • The venture’s impact
  • Scalability
  • Growth potential
  • The founder’s vision
  • The venture’s broader ambitions

Unlike the first-stage application, entrepreneurs cannot simply access the Invitational Application independently. It is reserved for ventures that have first been identified through the Eligibility Application process.

What Does Halcyon Look for in Applicants?

Halcyon states that its selection committee evaluates applications using four key criteria:

1. Impact

The first criterion is the potential of the venture to create meaningful positive impact.

Applicants should be able to clearly explain the problem they are addressing and why solving that problem matters.

A strong application should make it possible to understand:

  • What challenge the venture is addressing
  • Who is affected by the challenge
  • How the venture’s solution responds to the problem
  • What kind of positive change the venture seeks to create
  • How the impact can potentially be demonstrated or measured

The impact component is particularly important because Halcyon’s founder community is centred on businesses seeking to generate positive influence.

2. Scalability

Halcyon also considers the potential for a venture to grow.

Scalability involves demonstrating that the solution has the potential to expand beyond its current size, market or initial group of beneficiaries.

Applicants should therefore think carefully about questions such as:

  • Can the solution reach more people?
  • Can the business expand into additional markets?
  • What is the potential size of the problem being addressed?
  • What barriers could limit expansion?
  • What would growth look like over the next several years?

Entrepreneurs should present a realistic growth vision rather than simply stating that they intend to scale.

3. Innovation

Innovation is another central selection criterion.

Applicants should communicate what makes their approach different and why their solution offers a meaningful response to an existing challenge.

Innovation could relate to:

  • The technology being developed
  • The business model
  • The delivery model
  • The product or service
  • The way an existing problem is being approached
  • A new method of reaching underserved communities
  • A new way of generating measurable impact

The key is to demonstrate what is distinctive about the venture and how that distinction contributes to solving the identified problem.

4. Talent

The fourth criterion is talent.

This allows the selection committee to assess the people behind the venture, including their ability, experience, ambition and potential to execute the proposed vision.

Entrepreneurs should therefore make their application about more than just the product.

The application should also demonstrate:

  • Why the founders are equipped to address the problem
  • What relevant experience the team possesses
  • What the founders have already accomplished
  • How the team complements one another
  • Why the founders are committed to the venture
  • Why they have the ambition to grow the solution

Pitch Deck Is Now Required

One of the most important changes highlighted in the application information is that applicants are now required to upload a pitch deck of up to 15 slides.

This means entrepreneurs should prepare a clear and professionally structured pitch deck before submitting their application.

A strong pitch deck can help communicate the venture’s story in a way that is easy for the selection committee to understand.

While the specific content can vary depending on the venture, entrepreneurs may consider using their pitch deck to clearly present:

  1. The problem
  2. The target population or market
  3. The proposed solution
  4. How the solution works
  5. The innovation behind the approach
  6. The business or operating model
  7. Evidence of traction
  8. Impact achieved so far
  9. Growth and scalability potential
  10. Market opportunity
  11. Competitive landscape
  12. Team and relevant expertise
  13. Future growth strategy
  14. Financial or business milestones
  15. The long-term vision

Applicants should ensure that every slide adds useful information and supports the overall story of the venture.

Because the limit is 15 slides, entrepreneurs should avoid filling the presentation with excessive text.

The strongest deck structure is generally one in which the problem, solution, impact, traction, team and future opportunity can be understood quickly.

Optional One-Minute Video

In addition to the required pitch deck, applicants may also upload a one-minute video describing their venture.

Although the video is optional, it can provide an opportunity to communicate elements that may be difficult to convey through written answers alone.

The video can help founders demonstrate:

  • Their passion for the problem they are solving
  • Their vision for the venture
  • Their ability to communicate clearly
  • The human story behind the business
  • Why the problem matters
  • Why they are committed to creating positive impact

A one-minute video should remain focused.

Rather than attempting to explain every detail of the business, founders can use the limited time to communicate the core problem, the solution, the impact and their vision.

Why the Year-Round Application Matters

One of the biggest changes in Halcyon’s process is the move away from a traditional fixed application cycle for the initial eligibility stage.

Previously, entrepreneurs might have had to wait for a particular fellowship application to open before submitting their venture for consideration.

The new model allows founders to submit the Eligibility Application at any time during the year.

This means entrepreneurs can begin the process when they are ready rather than waiting for a specific fellowship deadline.

It also allows Halcyon to connect eligible ventures with future fellowships that are relevant to their areas of work.

For founders developing impact-driven businesses, this can make the application process more flexible.

There Is No Fixed Annual Deadline for Step 1

Unlike many fellowship and accelerator opportunities, the Halcyon Eligibility Application does not have a single annual deadline.

The application is described as being open year-round, with submissions reviewed on a rolling basis.

Therefore, the opportunity is particularly useful for founders who may not currently be ready for a particular fellowship but want their venture to be considered for future programmes.

However, applicants should understand the distinction between the two stages:

  • Step 1: Open year-round
  • Step 2: Opens only by invitation when an aligned fellowship becomes available

The absence of a fixed deadline for Step 1 does not mean that every venture will automatically progress to Step 2.

What Happens If Your Venture Is Not Selected?

Halcyon’s process also provides an important clarification for applicants.

If a venture is not selected during the Eligibility Application stage, Halcyon indicates that the venture is not considered a fit for any of its fellowships based on the eligibility assessment.

This makes the first-stage application an important screening process rather than simply a registration form.

Entrepreneurs should therefore take time to understand Halcyon’s eligibility requirements before submitting their application.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The Halcyon Open Application is designed for founders and ventures, rather than individual applicants seeking traditional educational scholarships or employment opportunities.

It is particularly relevant to entrepreneurs who are developing businesses or solutions with a clear impact mission.

Potential applicants may include founders working on solutions related to areas such as

  • Climate
  • Health
  • Equity
  • Social innovation
  • Environmental sustainability
  • Technology for positive impact
  • Economic inclusion
  • Community development
  • Other significant social or environmental challenges

The exact areas of focus can depend on the fellowship programme that becomes available.

Halcyon’s past programming has included ventures from multiple countries and regions. For example, its 2024 Climate Fellowship received applications from 69 countries across all continents except Antarctica, demonstrating the international reach of its fellowship programming.

However, applicants should distinguish this historical cohort information from the eligibility requirements of a specific future fellowship.

How to Prepare a Strong Halcyon Application

Entrepreneurs interested in applying should begin preparing well before submitting their Eligibility Application.

1. Clearly define the problem.

Start by identifying the specific problem the venture is addressing.

Avoid using broad statements that do not demonstrate the scale or nature of the problem.

Instead, explain:

  • What the problem is
  • Who experiences it
  • Why existing approaches are insufficient
  • How significant the problem is
  • What evidence demonstrates the need for your solution

2. Explain your solution clearly.

The selection committee needs to understand what the venture actually does.

Explain the product, service, technology or business model in straightforward language.

Avoid unnecessary technical terminology unless it is essential to understanding the innovation.

3. Demonstrate impact

Since impact is one of Halcyon’s four stated selection criteria, founders should provide evidence where possible.

Examples could include:

  • Number of people reached
  • Communities served
  • Revenue generated while delivering impact
  • Environmental outcomes
  • Health outcomes
  • Educational outcomes
  • Jobs created
  • Improvements in access or affordability
  • Partnerships established
  • Other measurable results

4. Demonstrate traction

If the venture is already operating, provide evidence showing what has been achieved.

This could include:

  • Customers
  • Users
  • Revenue
  • Partnerships
  • Pilot programmes
  • Contracts
  • Product launches
  • Geographic expansion
  • Investment
  • Awards
  • Measurable impact

Founders at an earlier stage should explain what has already been validated and what evidence supports the business model.

5. Explain the innovation.

Don’t simply describe the venture as innovative.

Explain why it is innovative.

Identify the specific element that distinguishes the venture from existing solutions.

6. Demonstrate scalability

Explain what growth could look like.

Applicants should show that they have thought about:

  • Market size
  • Customer growth
  • Geographic expansion
  • Operational capacity
  • Partnerships
  • Technology
  • Funding requirements
  • Team growth
  • Potential barriers to expansion

7. Introduce the founding team.

Use the application and pitch deck to explain why the team is capable of executing the vision.

Highlight relevant:

  • Professional experience
  • Technical skills
  • Entrepreneurial experience
  • Industry knowledge
  • Community experience
  • Previous achievements

8. Prepare the pitch deck carefully.

Because the pitch deck is now required and is limited to 15 slides, founders should make every slide purposeful.

The deck should tell a coherent story rather than functioning as a collection of unrelated information.

9. Consider adding the one-minute video.

The optional video can add personality to the application and allow founders to communicate their motivation directly.

Keep it concise, authentic and focused on the venture.

10. Submit only once.

Because duplicate Eligibility Applications are automatically rejected, founders should carefully review their information before pressing submit.

Check:

  • Spelling
  • Contact information
  • Venture information
  • Impact figures
  • Links
  • Pitch deck
  • Supporting information
  • Consistency between the application and pitch deck

Halcyon Open Application: Key Information

Application Process at a Glance

Entrepreneurs can follow these steps:

Step 1: Review eligibility

Before submitting anything, review Halcyon’s eligibility requirements and determine whether your venture fits the organisation’s programmes.

Step 2: Prepare your venture information

Gather information about:

  • Your mission
  • Venture stage
  • Impact
  • Innovation
  • Scalability
  • Founding team
  • Vision

Step 3: Prepare your pitch deck.

Create a pitch deck of no more than 15 slides, as required by the current application process.

Step 4: Consider recording the optional video

Prepare a one-minute video that introduces the venture and communicates the founders’ passion and vision.

Step 5: Submit the Eligibility Application

Submit the first-stage application through Halcyon’s application platform.

Remember that the Eligibility Application can only be submitted once.

Step 6: Wait for the rolling review

Halcyon reviews Eligibility Applications on a rolling basis.

Step 7: Await a potential invitation

If the venture meets the criteria and a suitable fellowship opens, Halcyon may invite the founder to complete the more detailed Invitational Application.

Step 8: Complete the Invitational Application

If invited, provide more detailed information about the venture, team, innovation, scalability, impact and vision.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does the Halcyon Open Application have a deadline?

There is no fixed deadline stated for the Eligibility Application. The application is open year-round and reviewed on a rolling basis.

However, individual fellowship programmes may have their own application windows and requirements.

Can I apply more than once?

No. Halcyon states that the Eligibility Application can only be submitted once. Duplicate applications are automatically rejected.

Is the second application open to everyone?

No. The second-stage Invitational Application is by invitation only.

Is a pitch deck required?

Yes. The current application information states that applicants are required to upload a pitch deck of up to 15 slides.

Is the one-minute video mandatory?

No. The one-minute video is optional.

What does Halcyon look for?

The selection committee evaluates applications using four criteria: Impact, Scalability, Innovation and Talent.

Is this an individual scholarship?

No. This opportunity is designed for entrepreneurs and impact-driven ventures seeking consideration for Halcyon’s fellowship programmes.

Can international founders apply?

Halcyon’s fellowship programming has demonstrated an international reach, including applicants and fellows from numerous countries. However, eligibility can vary by specific fellowship, so founders should check the requirements for the fellowship to which they are ultimately invited. Halcyon’s 2024 Climate Fellowship, for example, received applications from 69 countries across all continents except Antarctica.

Conclusion

The Halcyon Open Application provides impact-driven entrepreneurs with a flexible way to introduce their ventures to Halcyon throughout the year. Rather than requiring founders to wait for a specific annual application window, Halcyon has introduced a two-step model beginning with an Eligibility Application that remains open year-round.

The first stage focuses on determining whether a venture is a potential fit based on its mission, stage and impact focus. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, while ventures that meet the criteria may later be invited to complete a more comprehensive application when an appropriate fellowship becomes available.

Applicants should pay particular attention to Halcyon’s four selection criteria: Impact, Scalability, Innovation and Talent. The current process also requires applicants to submit a pitch deck of up to 15 slides, while a one-minute video may be included as an optional way to communicate the venture’s story and the founders’ vision.

There is no fixed deadline for the year-round Eligibility Application, but applicants should remember that the application can only be submitted once and duplicate submissions are automatically rejected.

For entrepreneurs building businesses intended to address significant social, environmental or other impact challenges, the application provides a route into consideration for Halcyon’s future fellowship opportunities. Because specific fellowships can have different requirements, applicants should review the applicable eligibility conditions carefully and ensure that their venture’s mission, stage and impact align with the programme for which they may ultimately be considered.

item.content:encoded:
Star Catcher is offering paid, full-time Summer 2027 internships for undergraduate students, graduate students, and recent graduates interested in contributing to the development of next-generation space energy infrastructure. The internship program provides participants with an opportunity to gain practical experience at a high-growth space technology company working toward building what it describes as the first power grid in space.

Applications are currently open for available Summer 2027 internship positions, with opportunities spanning engineering, science, business, marketing, communications, and related disciplines. Successful interns will work on real-world challenges, collaborate with experienced professionals, and contribute to projects involving the systems and infrastructure needed to support an emerging orbital economy.

Deadline: November 15, 2026.

About the Star Catcher Summer 2027 Internship Program

The Star Catcher internship program is designed for students and recent graduates who want to move beyond classroom learning and gain hands-on experience in the rapidly developing space technology sector.

As an intern, you will have the opportunity to participate in work that directly contributes to Star Catcher’s efforts to develop space-based power infrastructure. Rather than being limited to observational or administrative responsibilities, the program emphasizes practical work, rapid learning, ownership, and exposure to real engineering and operational challenges.

The company is seeking students from a broad range of academic and professional backgrounds. This makes the program relevant not only to traditional aerospace and engineering students, but also to candidates studying computer science, physics, business, marketing, communications, and related fields.

The internships are paid and full-time, giving selected candidates the opportunity to gain professional experience while working alongside teams involved in building emerging space technology.

What Will Interns Work On?

Star Catcher describes its mission as building the systems needed to establish a power grid in space. Interns will therefore have the opportunity to contribute to work connected to space technology, engineering, business operations, communications, and the development of the company’s broader commercial direction.

Depending on the position, interns may become involved in:

  • Engineering systems and technologies designed for space-based power infrastructure.
  • Research and technical problem-solving.
  • Development and analysis of spacecraft-related systems.
  • Software and computational projects.
  • Optical and electrical engineering applications.
  • Business development activities.
  • Market research and analysis.
  • Proposal development.
  • Marketing initiatives.
  • Corporate and external communications.
  • Content creation and storytelling.
  • Event organization.
  • Graphic design and visual communications.
  • Photography and videography.
  • Motion graphics and other creative projects.
  • Cross-functional projects involving multiple teams.

The specific responsibilities will depend on the internship position and the applicant’s academic background, skills, and experience.

Available Internship Areas

Star Catcher is looking for qualified undergraduate and graduate students to work across several disciplines. The available areas include:

1. Aerospace Engineering

Aerospace Engineering interns can gain experience working in an industry focused on spacecraft and space-based infrastructure. Candidates with an interest in spacecraft systems, aerospace technologies, and related engineering challenges may find this area particularly relevant.

2. Mechanical Engineering

Mechanical Engineering students can contribute their technical knowledge to projects involving mechanical systems and components. The role may provide exposure to the practical application of mechanical engineering principles in the space industry.

3. Electrical Engineering

Electrical Engineering opportunities are aimed at students interested in electrical systems and technologies supporting space-based infrastructure. This area can provide practical experience applying electrical engineering knowledge to real-world space technology challenges.

4. Optical Engineering

Optical Engineering interns can contribute to work involving optical systems and technologies relevant to space applications. This opportunity is particularly suited to students with an academic or project background in optical engineering or closely related disciplines.

5. Computer Science

Computer Science students can explore opportunities involving software, programming, computational problem-solving, and technology development. Candidates with experience in programming languages and technical tools may be able to apply their skills to practical space technology projects.

6. Physics

Physics students can apply analytical and scientific knowledge to real-world problems within the space technology environment. The discipline provides a foundation for understanding and addressing technical challenges associated with advanced space systems.

7. Marketing and Communications

The program also includes opportunities for students studying or experienced in Marketing and Communications.

Candidates in this area may work on activities such as:

  • Market research.
  • Writing and content development.
  • Communications.
  • Marketing campaigns.
  • Event organization.
  • Graphic design.
  • Photography and videography.
  • Motion graphics.
  • Other communication and creative projects.

This makes the program relevant to students who want to combine communication, creativity, technology, and the rapidly developing space industry.

8. Business Development

Business Development interns can gain exposure to commercial and strategic activities within a high-growth technology company. Candidates interested in identifying opportunities, researching markets, developing proposals, and supporting business growth may be considered for relevant positions.

Who Can Apply?

Star Catcher is seeking qualified undergraduate and graduate students of all backgrounds, as well as recent graduates.

Applicants should currently be pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in one of the relevant disciplines or have recently graduated from a related program.

Relevant fields include:

  • Aerospace Engineering
  • Mechanical Engineering
  • Electrical Engineering
  • Optical Engineering
  • Computer Science
  • Physics
  • Marketing
  • Communications
  • Business Administration
  • Related academic fields

Recent graduates may also qualify, depending on the requirements of the particular internship position.

Applicants should carefully review the individual position description before applying because specific requirements may vary between engineering, business development, marketing, and communications opportunities.

U.S. Citizenship and Space Technology Export Requirements

An important eligibility consideration applies to these internships because of the nature of the company’s space technology work.

Applicants must meet the applicable U.S. government authorization requirements for access to regulated space technology. According to the provided internship information, candidates must be one of the following:

  • A U.S. citizen;
  • A lawful permanent resident of the United States;
  • A protected individual as defined under 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3); or
  • An individual eligible to obtain the necessary authorizations from the U.S. Department of State to comply with U.S. government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR).

Therefore, international applicants should not assume that being enrolled in a relevant degree program automatically makes them eligible. Applicants should carefully assess their ability to satisfy the applicable export-control and authorization requirements before submitting an application.

What Experience Does Star Catcher Look For?

Academic qualifications are important, but Star Catcher is also looking for candidates who can demonstrate practical experience, technical ability, communication skills, and an interest in space, technology, and innovation.

Ideal candidates may have some combination of the following:

Previous Internship or Project Experience

Previous internship experience can demonstrate that an applicant has already had exposure to professional environments. Hands-on academic, personal, technical, or extracurricular projects may also help demonstrate the ability to turn theoretical knowledge into practical results.

Strong Communication Skills

Interns will work with other people and may need to communicate technical or business information clearly. Strong written and verbal communication skills can therefore be valuable across both technical and non-technical positions.

Organizational Skills

Because interns may work on projects with deadlines and multiple responsibilities, strong organizational and time-management skills can help candidates perform effectively.

Independent and Collaborative Working Skills

Star Catcher is seeking people who can work independently while also contributing effectively within team-oriented environments. Applicants should be prepared to demonstrate that they can take ownership of assigned responsibilities while collaborating with colleagues.

Analytical and Problem-Solving Skills

The ability to analyze problems, identify potential solutions, and approach unfamiliar challenges systematically is important for an internship focused on developing new technologies and business opportunities.

Engineering Skills and Technical Experience

Candidates applying for engineering positions are expected to have relevant technical knowledge and experience.

Depending on the position, useful experience may include proficiency with engineering and technical tools such as:

  • MATLAB
  • SolidWorks
  • Python
  • CAD software
  • Other engineering software tools

Familiarity with spacecraft systems is also identified as relevant experience for engineering candidates.

Applicants should therefore emphasize relevant university projects, laboratory work, research, engineering competitions, personal projects, software experience, and previous internships where applicable.

Marketing, Communications and Business Development Skills

Candidates interested in non-engineering roles can also demonstrate their suitability through academic coursework and practical experience.

Relevant experience may include:

  • Market research.
  • Proposal development.
  • Professional writing.
  • Content creation.
  • Marketing.
  • Corporate communications.
  • Event organization.
  • Graphic design.
  • Photography.
  • Videography.
  • Motion graphics.
  • Business development.
  • Communication strategy.
  • Digital content production.

Candidates should demonstrate how their previous experiences have helped them develop practical skills that can be applied in a professional environment.

Why Consider an Internship at Star Catcher?

The program provides an opportunity to gain professional experience in an emerging area of the space industry while contributing to projects at a high-growth startup.

According to Star Catcher, interns can benefit from several aspects of the experience.

Direct Exposure to Industry Professionals

Interns will have an opportunity to work around experienced professionals and gain exposure to people working on advanced space technology and business challenges.

This can help students understand how concepts learned through university studies are applied in an actual technology company.

Build Frontier Technology

The internship offers the opportunity to contribute to technology being developed for a relatively new area of the space industry.

For students interested in aerospace, engineering, computing, physics, communications, business, or technology, this type of experience can provide insight into how emerging technologies move from concepts and research toward practical applications.

Work on Foundational Space Infrastructure

Star Catcher describes its mission as developing next-generation space energy infrastructure. Interns therefore have the opportunity to join a company at an early stage of development and contribute to foundational work.

This may provide valuable exposure to the challenges of building new products, systems, operations, and business functions within a rapidly developing company.

Gain Space Industry Experience

For students hoping to establish careers in the space sector, practical industry experience can provide an opportunity to develop professional skills and gain a better understanding of how the sector operates.

The interdisciplinary nature of the internships also means that space industry careers are not limited to engineering and science. Marketing, communications, business development, and other professional functions are also important to technology companies operating in the space sector.

Application Timeline

Applicants should pay close attention to the recruitment timeline.

Application deadline: November 15, 2026

Following the application period:

  • November–December 2026: Interviews are expected to take place.
  • Early 2027: Internship offers are expected to be extended.
  • Summer 2027: Selected interns are expected to participate in the internship program.

Applicants are encouraged to submit their applications before the deadline rather than waiting until the final day.

How to Apply for Star Catcher Summer 2027 Internships

There are separate application routes depending on the type of position you are interested in.

Engineering Internships

Students interested in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Optical Engineering, Computer Science, Physics, and related technical positions can review the available engineering opportunities and submit their applications through the engineering internship application page.

Marketing and Communications Internships

Students interested in Marketing, Communications, content creation, graphic design, photography, videography, motion graphics, and related areas can review the available Marketing and Communications internship opportunities.

Applicants should carefully read the complete job description for the specific position before submitting an application.

APPLY HERE

Tips for Preparing a Strong Application

Applicants can improve their preparation by tailoring their application to the specific internship rather than submitting a generic application.

Highlight Relevant Projects

Students who have limited professional experience can use academic and personal projects to demonstrate their capabilities.

Engineering candidates could highlight design projects, programming projects, laboratory work, spacecraft-related research, CAD projects, or other technical work.

Marketing and communications candidates could highlight campaigns, articles, social media projects, graphic design work, videos, photography, event projects, websites, or other relevant portfolio pieces.

Demonstrate Technical Skills

Engineering applicants should clearly identify relevant software and technical skills rather than simply stating that they have “computer skills.”

For example, experience with Python, MATLAB, CAD, SolidWorks, or other engineering tools can be specifically identified where applicable.

Show Practical Experience

Previous internships, volunteer work, university projects, student organizations, competitions, freelance work, research, and other hands-on experiences can help demonstrate initiative and practical ability.

Tailor Your Application

Applicants should connect their qualifications to the responsibilities of the position they are applying for.

A candidate applying for a communications internship, for example, should emphasize relevant communication, writing, content creation, marketing, graphic design, photography, videography, or event experience.

An engineering applicant should instead focus on technical projects, engineering tools, analytical skills, research, and spacecraft or related engineering experience.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Star Catcher Summer 2027 Paid Internships.

Conclusion

The Star Catcher Summer 2027 Paid Internships provide an opportunity for students and recent graduates to gain practical experience while contributing to an ambitious space technology initiative. The program covers a wide range of disciplines, from Aerospace, Mechanical, Electrical and Optical Engineering to Computer Science and Physics, as well as Marketing, Communications and Business Development.

The internships are particularly relevant for candidates who want hands-on experience, enjoy solving real-world problems, and are interested in the intersection of technology, innovation and the emerging space economy. Engineering applicants can demonstrate their capabilities through technical projects and software experience, while Marketing, Communications and Business Development applicants can showcase relevant coursework, professional experience, creative work and practical projects.

However, applicants should pay close attention to the program’s eligibility requirements, particularly the U.S. government authorization requirements associated with space technology export regulations.

item.content:encoded:
The Maria Rosario Lazzati Niada Scholarship for Afghan Women is now accepting applications for the 2027–2028 academic year, offering an important postgraduate study opportunity for talented Afghan women who hold a university degree and wish to advance their knowledge in international relations and development.

The scholarship is offered in memory of Maria Rosario Lazzati Niada and supports successful candidates to undertake a two-year master’s programme at the Geneva Graduate Institute in Switzerland. The scholarship provides CHF 25,000 per year, making it a substantial source of financial support for an eligible scholar pursuing graduate education abroad.

The application deadline for the scholarship is 11:59 PM on October 26, 2026.

Maria Rosario Lazzati Niada Scholarship for Afghan Women

The Maria Rosario Lazzati Niada Scholarship was established to support talented Afghan women with university-level education who want to further their academic knowledge and professional opportunities in the fields of international relations and development.

Successful scholarship beneficiaries will enrol in a two-year master’s programme at the Geneva Graduate Institute, a graduate institution based in Geneva, Switzerland. The scholarship is specifically designed around the educational needs and circumstances of Afghan women and seeks to expand opportunities for them to pursue university education abroad.

The Geneva Graduate Institute states that its master’s programmes can provide pathways toward careers in areas such as academia, diplomacy, international organisations, non-governmental organisations and international corporate organisations.

Scholarship Details at a Glance

Detail Information
Scholarship Name Maria Rosario Lazzati Niada Scholarship for Afghan Women
Academic Year 2027–2028
Study Level Postgraduate / Master’s
Duration Two years
Study Location Geneva, Switzerland
Institution Geneva Graduate Institute
Annual Scholarship Amount CHF 25,000
Field Focus International Relations and Development
Target Group Afghan women with a university degree
Scholarship Deadline October 26, 2026, at 11:59 PM
Institute Application Deadline for the Selected Candidate January 15
English Proficiency Required at the Geneva Graduate Institute application stage
Academic References Two required at the Geneva Graduate Institute application stage

The scholarship itself is awarded for two years. However, continuation into the second year is subject to the beneficiary preparing a report at the end of the first year and providing evidence of successful academic progress. The scholarship is then renewed based on this review.

What Is the Maria Rosario Lazzati Niada Scholarship?

The scholarship was created in memory of Maria Rosario Lazzati Niada (18 March 1954–2 February 2022). According to the Geneva Graduate Institute, Maria Rosario was a high school teacher of history and literature who graduated Magna Cum Laude from the State University of Milan with a degree in the History of Christianity.

Her academic interests included the condition of women. Her university thesis on witchcraft later developed into the book La Stregoneria, written with historians S. Abbiati and A. Agnoletto and published by Mondadori in 1984. The book examined persecution between the 13th and 17th centuries and was based on historical trial documents.

Her commitment to women’s education also extended beyond academic research.

In 2005, Maria Rosario played a major role in establishing the Comitato Arghosha Faraway Schools, a charity focused on women’s education in Afghanistan. The organisation subsequently supported the construction of 15 schools serving approximately 8,000 pupils from grades 1 to 12. According to the Geneva Graduate Institute, approximately 5,500 of these pupils were girls, while 10 of the schools were built specifically for girls who had little or no access to educational facilities.

The organisation also supported:

  • Literacy courses for approximately 500 adult women.
  • 28 university scholarships for talented girls at universities in Kabul.
  • The development and implementation of educational initiatives in different parts of Afghanistan.

Until 2019, Maria Rosario reportedly travelled to Afghanistan each year to assess the implementation of projects and help plan future initiatives.

The scholarship therefore continues a broader legacy centred on education and opportunities for Afghan women.

What Does the Scholarship Offer?

One of the most significant features of this opportunity is its financial support.

CHF 25,000 per year

The Maria Rosario Lazzati Niada Scholarship provides an annual scholarship amount of 25,000 Swiss francs. Since the scholarship is structured as a two-year award, it can provide substantial financial assistance throughout the master’s programme, subject to renewal for the second year.

The scholarship is particularly significant because it is designed to support eligible Afghan women pursuing postgraduate education outside Afghanistan.

Two years of master’s-level study

Successful candidates will undertake a two-year master’s programme at the Geneva Graduate Institute. The scholarship is therefore intended for candidates seeking advanced academic training rather than short-term training or undergraduate education.

Academic and professional development

The opportunity is focused on strengthening knowledge in international relations and development. The Institute notes that master’s-level education can create pathways into academic and diplomatic careers as well as employment with international organisations, non-governmental organisations and international companies.

Who Can Apply for the Maria Rosario Lazzati Niada Scholarship?

The scholarship is specifically intended for Afghan women who already hold a university degree and wish to pursue master’s-level studies.

The official scholarship description identifies the target applicants as talented Afghan women with a university degree who want to improve their knowledge in international relations and development.

Basic eligibility profile

Applicants should therefore fall within the following broad category:

  1. Women applicants
  2. Afghan applicants
  3. Applicants who hold a university degree
  4. Applicants interested in pursuing master’s-level study
  5. Applicants seeking further academic development in areas connected to international relations and development
  6. Applicants who can prepare the required scholarship application documentation.
  7. Applicants who, if selected by the scholarship committee, can subsequently complete the Geneva Graduate Institute admission process.

The official scholarship information does not state a particular race requirement. The eligibility criterion is specifically framed around being an Afghan woman, rather than race. In geographic terms, the opportunity is therefore targeted specifically at Afghan women, rather than being a scholarship open to women from all African, Asian, European or other continents.

There is also no age limit stated in the scholarship information provided by the Geneva Graduate Institute.

What Documents Are Required?

Applicants need to prepare several important documents before submitting their scholarship application.

According to the official 2027–2028 scholarship flyer, applicants must include:

1. Motivation letter

The motivation letter should explain several important aspects of the applicant’s plans.

It should cover:

  • Why the applicant is applying for the Maria Rosario Lazzati Niada Scholarship.
  • Which Geneva Graduate Institute master’s programme the applicant wants to pursue.
  • Why the applicant has selected the Geneva Graduate Institute.
  • The applicant’s financial needs.
  • The applicant’s plans after graduation.

A strong motivation letter should therefore connect the applicant’s educational background, proposed master’s programme, career objectives and financial circumstances in a coherent way.

2. Curriculum vitae

Applicants must submit a CV outlining their academic background, professional experience, relevant skills, achievements and other qualifications.

3. University diplomas and qualifications

Applicants must provide copies of their university diplomas and qualifications obtained.

This is particularly important because the scholarship is designed for women who already possess university-level education and are seeking postgraduate study.

4. Official academic transcripts

Applicants must also submit official academic transcripts showing their coursework, grades and the corresponding credit values.

Applicants should therefore ensure that their academic records are available before beginning the application process.

What Happens After the Scholarship Application?

The scholarship process has an important second stage.

The scholarship’s Steering Committee reviews applications and contacts candidates regarding the scholarship decision. The committee is composed of representatives from the Association Arghosha, the Geneva Graduate Institute and people of Afghan origin or with close ties to Afghanistan.

Importantly, being selected for the scholarship does not end the process.

The selected candidate must apply to the Geneva Graduate Institute

The scholarship’s Steering Committee will help prepare the successful candidate’s application file for the Geneva Graduate Institute.

The selected candidate must then apply to the Institute by January 15. The scholarship flyer specifically notes that the late application round does not apply to this process.

At this stage, the candidate will need to provide:

  • An English proficiency certificate.
  • Two academic references.

These are requested as part of the Geneva Graduate Institute application process.

Applicants with questions about study programmes or admission can contact the Geneva Graduate Institute through the admissions contact provided in the official information.

Important Application Deadlines

Applicants should pay close attention to the distinction between the scholarship application deadline and the subsequent Geneva Graduate Institute application deadline.

Scholarship application deadline

The deadline to submit the scholarship application is

October 26, 2026, at 11:59 PM (midnight).

Applicants should not wait until the final day if they still need to obtain transcripts, diplomas or other supporting documents.

Geneva Graduate Institute application deadline

After the Steering Committee selects its candidate, that candidate must submit the application to the Geneva Graduate Institute by:

January 15.

The Institute application is a separate stage and includes additional requirements, including an English proficiency certificate and two academic references.

Why This Opportunity Is Relevant to International Relations and Development Students

The scholarship is particularly relevant to Afghan women who want to develop careers connected to international affairs, diplomacy, development, international organisations or related fields.

A master’s degree from the Geneva Graduate Institute can provide advanced academic exposure to international issues and development-related subjects. The Institute itself identifies potential career pathways including academic and diplomatic careers, international and non-governmental organisations, and international corporate companies.

For an applicant interested in international relations, development, diplomacy or global affairs, the opportunity combines postgraduate study with an international academic environment in Geneva.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Applicants can improve the clarity of their applications by preparing each component carefully.

1. Research the master’s programme

Before writing the motivation letter, applicants should identify the specific master’s programme they want to pursue at the Geneva Graduate Institute.

The application asks candidates to explain which programme they would like to apply to and why they chose the Institute.

The motivation letter should therefore demonstrate that the applicant has a clear academic direction.

2. Explain the connection between education and career goals.

Applicants should clearly demonstrate how the proposed master’s programme fits into their longer-term professional plans.

For example, the application can explain how advanced study could contribute to the applicant’s ambitions in:

  • International relations
  • Diplomacy
  • International development
  • International organisations
  • Non-governmental organisations
  • Academia
  • International business or corporate organisations

These areas correspond with career pathways identified by the Geneva Graduate Institute.

3. Address financial need clearly.

Financial need is explicitly listed among the issues that applicants should address in their motivation letter.

Applicants should therefore explain their circumstances clearly and factually rather than treating financial need as a secondary part of the application.

4. Prepare academic records early.

Because the application requires university diplomas, qualifications and official transcripts, applicants should begin collecting these documents before the deadline.

This is particularly important where obtaining official transcripts or certified academic documents takes time.

5. Prepare for the second-stage admission process.

Applicants should also understand that scholarship selection and university admission are connected but distinct stages.

The selected scholarship candidate will subsequently need to apply to the Geneva Graduate Institute and provide an English proficiency certificate and two academic references.

Preparing these materials early can help avoid delays later in the process.

Application Process

The application process can be understood in two main stages.

Stage 1: Apply for the scholarship

Applicants submit their scholarship application with:

  1. Motivation letter
  2. Curriculum vitae
  3. Copies of university diplomas and qualifications
  4. Official academic transcripts

The scholarship application must be submitted by 11:59 PM on October 26, 2026.

Stage 2: Apply to the Geneva Graduate Institute

The Steering Committee reviews applications and selects its candidate. The selected candidate then proceeds with the Geneva Graduate Institute application.

That application must be submitted by January 15 and requires an English proficiency certificate and two academic references.

Applicants should therefore view the process as a sequence rather than assuming that submission of the scholarship application automatically completes the university admission process.

About the Geneva Graduate Institute

The Geneva Graduate Institute is a postgraduate institution based in Geneva, Switzerland, with an academic focus that includes international affairs and development.

The scholarship specifically places successful candidates into a two-year master’s programme at the Institute.

For Afghan women seeking to pursue postgraduate education internationally, the programme provides an opportunity to study in a major international city and develop knowledge relevant to global affairs and development.

Application Link

Eligible applicants interested in the Maria Rosario Lazzati Niada Scholarship for Afghan Women should submit their scholarship application through the official application form.

Apply for the Maria Rosario Lazzati Niada Scholarship

Applicants can also review the official scholarship information and application requirements through the Geneva Graduate Institute.

APPLY HERE

Key Facts About the Opportunity

  • Opportunity: Maria Rosario Lazzati Niada Scholarship for Afghan Women
  • Academic year: 2027–2028
  • Study level: Master’s degree
  • Duration: Two years
  • Institution: Geneva Graduate Institute
  • Location: Geneva, Switzerland
  • Scholarship value: CHF 25,000 annually
  • Target applicants: Talented Afghan women with a university degree
  • Academic focus: International relations and development
  • Scholarship application deadline: October 26, 2026, at 11:59 PM
  • Subsequent Institute application deadline for the selected candidate: January 15
  • Required scholarship documents: Motivation letter, CV, university diplomas/qualifications and official academic transcripts
  • Additional Institute-stage requirements: English proficiency certificate and two academic references
  • Programme: Two-year master’s programme
  • Renewal: Second-year scholarship continuation depends on satisfactory academic progress and submission of the required first-year report.

Visit HERE for more information about the Maria Rosario Lazzati Niada Scholarship for Afghan Women 2027–2028.

Conclusion

The Maria Rosario Lazzati Niada Scholarship for Afghan Women 2027–2028 offers a significant postgraduate education opportunity for eligible Afghan women who hold a university degree and want to advance their academic and professional knowledge in international relations and development.

The scholarship provides CHF 25,000 per year for a two-year master’s programme, subject to the conditions for renewal in the second year. Beyond the financial support, the opportunity provides access to postgraduate study at the Geneva Graduate Institute and an international academic environment in Geneva.

Applicants should pay particular attention to the October 26, 2026, deadline, ensure that all required academic documents are ready, and prepare a strong motivation letter addressing their chosen master’s programme, reasons for selecting the Institute, financial circumstances and plans after graduation.

For the selected scholarship candidate, the process continues with a separate Geneva Graduate Institute application by January 15, including an English proficiency certificate and two academic references.

For Afghan women who meet the stated requirements and are seeking postgraduate education in international relations, development or related areas, this scholarship represents an opportunity to pursue a two-year master’s education in Geneva with substantial annual financial support.
